id: title:EDsCODE:stop managed warehouse and dags edits fanning out tests

observations.code_quote: // A diff whose legacy edits are all Dagster Python also legitimately selects nothing.
observations.behavior: Adds a DAGSTER-only exemption to the Django selection decision; if every changed file is Dagster Python and no Django segment was selected, it returns an empty selection without running Django tests.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces unnecessary CI execution for pure Dagster changes while preserving existing behavior when non-Python or mixed files change.

observations.behavior: Checks that each identified Dagster Python file still exists before treating the whole set as exempt. Deleted files do not qualify for the exemption.
observations.posthog_connection: Prevents false positives where deleted Dagster files could incorrectly trigger the DAGSTER-only exemption in CI selection logic.

observations.behavior: Updates Playwright E2E workflow exclusion list to skip posthog/dags/ directory explicitly.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies that Dagster code does not participate in the E2E stack, preventing potential misclassification of test dependencies.

observations.limitations: Only three hunks reviewed out of P4 and P5 which contain warehouse-related facade import restructuring; tier assessment relies on P1 and P2 only.

review.limitations: Only three hunks reviewed out of P4 and P5 which contain warehouse-related facade import restructuring; tier assessment relies on P1 and P2 only.
review.reason: Adds a bounded correctness improvement: DAGSTER-only legacy edits are now recognized and excluded from Django test runs, supported by checks and documentation. This is substantive but localized to the selection decision and its supporting tests; no broader systemic risk reduction demonstrated across components.
review.posthog_relevance: Reduces unnecessary CI execution while preserving existing behavior when non-Python or mixed files change.
review.uncertainty: Assessment depends solely on P1 and P2; P4 and P5 changes involve warehouse facade imports and may carry additional relevance.
